findings.evidence: Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/SpecialLinearGroup.lean:956-967 tags the analogous row lemmas `T_pow_mul_apply_one`, `T_mul_apply_one` and `T_inv_mul_apply_one` with `@[simp]`.
findings.fix: Tag all three `@[simp]`. The right-hand side is a `![…]` literal, so they cannot loop.
findings.issue: `mul_S_apply`, `mul_T_zpow_apply` and `mul_T_apply` rewrite `(γ * S) i`, `(γ * T ^ n) i` and `(γ * T) i` to an explicit vector. That is the normal form, but none of them is `@[simp]`. Every use in Multiplier.lean, Kronecker.lean and Transformation.lean passes them by hand as `simp only [Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.mul_T_apply, Matrix.cons_val_zero, Matrix.cons_val_one]`.

findings.evidence: grep `exists_int_twelve_mul_dedekindSum|cast_dedekindSum|dedekindSum_eq_of_mul_modEq_one|etaMultiplier_eq_kroneckerEtaMultiplier` over code/TauCeti: no hits. Kronecker.lean: `private noncomputable def kroneckerEtaMultiplier`.
findings.fix: Rewrite the description to list only the declarations that actually exist: the `etaMultiplier_eq_*kroneckerSym*` family and `IsCoprime.ratCast_dedekindSum`. Drop the claims about the 24th-power integrality theorem and the public `kroneckerEtaMultiplier`, or add those declarations.
findings.issue: The description names these as main public declarations: `TauCeti.ModularForm.kroneckerEtaMultiplier`, `etaMultiplier_eq_kroneckerEtaMultiplier`, `TauCeti.exists_int_twelve_mul_dedekindSum`, `IsCoprime.cast_dedekindSum` and `dedekindSum_eq_of_mul_modEq_one`. Grepping `code/TauCeti` finds no `etaMultiplier_eq_kroneckerEtaMultiplier`, `exists_int_twelve_mul_dedekindSum`, `cast_dedekindSum` or `dedekindSum_eq_of_mul_modEq_one`, and `kroneckerEtaMultiplier` is a `private noncomputable def`. The actual Kronecker products are `etaMultiplier_eq_ite_kroneckerSym_mul_cexp` and its odd, even and coprime-to-6 variants, and the Dedekind-sum cast lemma is `IsCoprime.ratCast_dedekindSum`.

summary: The new SL(2,ℤ) row-entry lemmas lack the `@[simp]` that Mathlib gives its analogues, so every consumer has to spell them out in `simp only`. The PR description also lists public declarations that do not exist in the diff, so it misstates the post-PR interface.
